Let's analyze the exact values from Wikipedia. In the infobox of the Wikipedia page for the Moon, under `periapsis` (perigee): `| periapsis = {{gaps |362 |600}} km
({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km)` So the range of perigee given in the infobox is: 356,400 km to 370,400 km (average 362,600 km). The prompt asks: "Please use the minimum perigee value on the Wikipedia page for the Moon when carrying out your calculation." So minimum perigee value = 356,400 km (or 356400 km). Now let's verify Eliud Kipchoge's record-making marathon pace / world record on Wikipedia. Let's query Kipchoge's world record from Wikipedia. Wait! What is Kipchoge's record-making marathon pace / world record marathon time? Let's check Kipchoge's official world record marathon time (set in 2022 at Berlin: 2:01:09, or 2:01:39 set in 2018). Wait! What is the marathon distance? Official marathon distance is 42.195 km (or 26 miles 385 yards = 42.195 km). Wait, does Eliud Kipchoge have a world record marathon time listed on Wikipedia? Let's check Kipchoge's wikitext for world record details or personal bests! Let's write a python snippet to pull Kipchoge's infobox and personal bests from wikitext. ```python cmd = """python -c " import urllib.request, json req = urllib.request.Request('https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&rvprop=content&format=json&titles=Eliud_Kipchoge', headers={'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'}) content = list(json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req).read())['query']['pages'].values())[0]['revisions'][0]['*'] for line in content.splitlines(): if 'marathon' in line.lower() or 'record' in line.lower(): print(line) " """ res = await run_command(cmd) print(res) ```
